Quote source · Q0120

Who said “Truth happens to an idea. It becomes true, is made true by events”?

The located source for this passage, the original-language wording where one exists, and the forms of it that circulate without the attribution.

Quote source / William James / Truth happens to an idea.…

English

Truth happens to an idea. It becomes true, is made true by events.
Thinker William James
Work Pragmatism
School Pragmatism
Theme Truth

Checked against the cited edition on 2026-09-14.

The recorded source

Attributed to
William James
Work and locator
Pragmatism
English wording
“Truth happens to an idea. It becomes true, is made true by events.”
Original wording (English)
Truth happens to an idea. It becomes true, is made true by events.

Two sentences, from Lecture VI, “Pragmatism's Conception of Truth,” in Pragmatism (1907). The second sentence is what the first means.

Exact wording and the variants in circulation

A quotation in English from a non-English source has two versions, and they are not interchangeable.

The wording recorded here is the one this archive holds. These are the forms that circulate in its place:

  • “Truth happens to an idea.”
  • “Truth is what happens to an idea.”

Attribution notes

Quoted at the first sentence alone it reads as relativism — as if anything could become true. James' argument is the opposite: an idea is made true by its verification in events, so the second sentence is not an elaboration but the claim itself. Cutting it off is the single most common way this passage is misrepresented, and readers who arrive looking for the source are usually looking because the one-sentence version seemed to say something James would have denied.
